title: Does b = a make a second list?
hook: Two names, one list. Change it through one name and look at the other.

knows: assigning a value to a variable
doesNotKnow: that assigning a list copies the name, not the list

misconception: b = a makes a separate copy of the list.
objective: The learner can say that after b = a both names point at one list, so appending through b changes what a shows, and that a copy is needed to get a separate list.

claims.text: After a = [1, 2], b = a and b.append(3), a is [1, 2, 3].
claims.source: Node: let a=[1,2]; let b=a; b.push(3); JSON.stringify(a) = [1,2,3] and a === b is true. Same in Python (list assignment binds a second name). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 9): Python: a=[1,2]; b=a; b.append(3) gives a == [1,2,3] (assignment binds a name, Python Language Reference 7.2). Stage question matches.

claims.text: Assigning a list gives a second name for the same list; it does not copy the list.
claims.source: Python Language Reference, Data model and Assignment statements: assignment binds a name to an object. ECMAScript spec: arrays are objects and assignment copies the reference. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 9): Python Language Reference s.7.2 (assignment binds names to objects; no copy). Reveal says 'copies the name, not the list', same meaning.

claims.text: After b is given a copy of a, appending through either name leaves the other list unchanged.
claims.source: Node: let a2=[1,2]; let c=[...a2]; c.push(3); a2 stays [1,2], c is [1,2,3]. The stage shows the copy as a separate box. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 9): Python: b = a.copy(); b.append(3) leaves a == [1,2]. Demo.tsx gives b its own list after copy and the 'held' readout shows the other list unchanged.

claims.text: To get a separate list you must copy it.
claims.source: Python docs, copy module and list.copy(); MDN spread syntax / Array.prototype.slice. Scope: a shallow copy of a list of numbers. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 9): Python docs: list.copy() / copy module give a new list (shallow, sufficient for a list of ints).

claims.text: The stage's names, arrows and boxes show two names pointing at one list or at two lists.
claims.source: Model drawing: arrows from the name tags a and b to list boxes, drawn from the same state that the readouts show. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 9): Demo.tsx: arrow end y (aY, bY) and the second Box are drawn from 'aliased' = bPoints === 0, the same state as the readouts.

recall.question: x = [5]. y = x. y.append(6). What is x?
recall.why: y = x gives the list a second name, so appending through y changes the one list that x also points at.
